# University of Melbourne Summary
The University of Melbourne, established in 1853 in Victoria, Australia, is one of the nation’s oldest and most prestigious institutions. Initially founded to award degrees in arts, medicine, law, and music, it quickly expanded to include faculties such as law (1857), engineering (1861), and medicine (1862). The university experienced substantial growth throughout the 20th and 21st centuries, both academically and physically, notably absorbing additional colleges and research institutes, and introducing the impactful Melbourne Model in 2008, which restructured undergraduate education into generalist degrees followed by specialised graduate courses. Research activity is robust, with the university consistently ranking first nationally and among the top 40 globally, maintaining Australia's largest cohort of research students, and housing numerous research centres. Its endowment stands at approximately $1.3 billion, and the university is known for significant fundraising campaigns and ongoing capital works.
The University is situated on the Parkville campus in central Melbourne, with further campuses at Burnley (horticulture), Southbank (arts and music), Werribee (veterinary science), Creswick (forestry), Dookie (agriculture), and Shepparton (rural health). A major new campus focusing on engineering is set for Fishermans Bend, opening in 2026. The university operates under a 13-member Council and is divided into nine faculties, offering a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs. International students make up 44% of the student body, and Melbourne is prominent for its residential college system and vibrant student life, including numerous clubs, associations, and sporting achievements. Melbourne boasts many notable alumni and staff, including multiple Nobel laureates and several Australian prime ministers. In recent years, controversies over governance, workplace culture, and protest handling have attracted scrutiny. Emma Johnston is set to become the first female Vice-Chancellor in 2025.
